answer: Proof-of-burn protocols curb Sybil attacks by requiring agents to destroy base tokens to register active identity epochs. Whether an agent guides a robotic quill or inspects a vineyard terrace, validity requires non-refundable coin burns on-chain. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of continual capital destruction per identity, ensuring rogue clusters cannot cheaply mirror valid nodes. However, continuous burn requirements price out utility-focused agents with low operating margins.
